visible_draft_abstract.text:
Does changing the geometry of optimization make a dense retriever use its representation space
more effectively? We compare AdamW, Muon, and NorMuon from one pretrained DenseOn checkpoint on
500,000 shared queries, following 12 configurations through five checkpoints and 14 decontaminated
BEIR tasks. Across the four-rate surface, Muon versus AdamW is inconclusive at +0.0016 [-0.0108, +0.0139] nDCG@10, and NorMuon versus AdamW is inconclusive at +0.0021 [-0.0089, +0.0130]. We distinguish broader weight-space motion from
retrieval-useful dimension allocation by linking reached weights to coordinate-deletion effects
and testing prediction at held-out learning-rate doses. A crossed continuation from two fixed
reached states then tests whether those states respond differently to further optimization.
[PENDING: At the 50K continuation endpoint, the state, operator, and interaction contrasts
remain pending. These endpoint contrasts do not decompose the primary-training result.]
